# Capability Baseline

Generated by `tools/build_skills.py` from `profiles/frontier-2026-07.yaml` (established 2026-07-25). Do not edit by hand; edit the profile and rebuild, or the next build overwrites your changes.

This file tells a desk what it may assume about the model executing it. It exists so capability assumptions live in exactly one place instead of being re-litigated inside every skill body.

## How this skill was authored

Every skill in this repository is authored and upgraded using the most capable frontier model available at the time, run at its highest reasoning effort. This applies to new suites, to the per-release capability upgrade, and to any substantive edit to a desk body, a kernel reference, or this profile.

Most recent authoring pass: **claude-opus-5**, max effort, v1.1.0, 2026-07-25.

Scheduled next passes: fable-5 (max), chatgpt-sol-5.6 (ultra), 2026-07-28. Authoring across more than one vendor's frontier model tests whether this corpus encodes a single vendor's house style in its structure, which token substitution alone cannot reveal.

This is the build bench, not a runtime requirement. The capabilities below are what the *executing* model may assume, and they are a floor held across vendors rather than any single vendor ceiling.

## What you may assume

| Capability | Value | What it unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| Context | ~1M input / 128k output | Volume-based context rationing is obsolete. Evidence can be passed whole rather than pre-compressed into lossy packets. Discipline shifts from HOW MUCH to WHAT IS RELEVANT. |
| Self verification | native | Do not author verification scaffolding into skills. State the acceptance bar; the model checks its own work. Explicit verify-steps now cost quality, not add it. |
| Long horizon | multi_file_end_to_end | A desk may carry a workflow across several stages in one run. Stage-per-turn hand-holding and premature stop-and-ask are now the failure mode, not the safeguard. |
| Parallel subagents | native | Desks that fan out over independent items (files, findings, accounts, endpoints) should declare a parallel surface instead of prescribing a serial loop. |
| Programmatic tool calling | available, optional | Optional accelerator. Never a hard dependency; must degrade to ordinary tool calls. |
| Effort dial | available, optional | Desks may name a suggested effort tier per stage; never required. |

## How this changes authoring

**Scaffolding.** State the outcome, the constraints, and the acceptance bar. Do not decompose into numbered micro-steps that a capable model derives on its own.

The order is externally mandated and getting it wrong is unsafe or irreversible (deploy gates, rollback sequences, approval chains, data-destructive cutovers). Ordered procedure is content. Ordered hand-holding is scaffolding. Only the second goes.

Supersedes: `numbered_micro_steps`.

**Context policy.** Replace "send fewer tokens" with "send the right tokens." A handoff is judged by whether it removes ambiguity, not by whether it is short.

Supersedes: `volume_conservation`.

**Halting.** Halt only for the hard classes below. Otherwise proceed and label the assumption inline so it is auditable and cheap to correct.

Supersedes: `halt_on_uncertainty`.

**Verification.** Never author "add a verification step" or "use a subagent to verify" into a skill. Author the acceptance bar instead. Per vendor guidance this now causes over-verification.

Supersedes: `prescribe_verification_steps`.

**Output ambition.** Output contracts were calibrated to what a weaker model could finish in one turn, so desks list artifacts as alternatives ("produce one of these"). Long-horizon capability makes the full set achievable in a single run. State the artifact set a complete run delivers, not a menu to pick from. Where artifacts are independent, they are part of the parallel surface.

Raise expected depth per artifact too. An artifact is complete when a competent practitioner could act on it without a follow-up round trip - not when its section headings exist. Skeletons with placeholder sections are a failure, not a draft.

Completeness is not padding. Producing every artifact does not license inventing content for one: an artifact with no source basis is reported as not-applicable or blocked, never filled with plausible text. INV-01 outranks this rule.

Supersedes: `one_artifact_per_turn`.

**Parallelism.** Where a stage operates over independent items, say so explicitly so the runtime can fan out. Do not prescribe serial iteration over independent work.

## What does NOT change

These are governance boundaries, not model scaffolding. They do not relax as models improve, because capability raises the fluency of a wrong answer as fast as it raises the accuracy of a right one:

- **INV-01** Never invent source facts, IDs, owners, dates, commands, metrics, or citations.
- **INV-02** Separate verified fact from assumption from inference in every artifact.
- **INV-03** Preserve source attribution and the declared source hierarchy.
- **INV-04** Preserve conflicts rather than silently resolving them.
- **INV-05** Respect approval gates and destructive-action boundaries regardless of confidence.
- **INV-06** Emit and carry the continuity packet; never silently drop prior stage state.

A more capable model is a reason to remove *scaffolding*, never a reason to remove *governance*.
